correctness.rationale: PASS. The falling-factorial 2-adic series F(x)=sum_j (-1)^j P_j(x) converges uniformly because products of j consecutive 2-adic integers have at least floor(j/2) factors of two; its derivative converges uniformly and the integral Taylor remainder gives F(x+h)-F(x)=hF'(x) modulo h^2. From F(x+1)=1-(x+1)F(x) and F'(0)=-sum_{m>=0}m! ≡2 mod4, parity branches have v2(F'(odd))=0, v2(F'(even))=1. For odd x and h divisible2 the linear term dominates; for same even x mod4 and h divisible4 it also dominates with +1 valuation. Hence H(t)=F(1+2t)/2 and G0/G2=(F(4t)-1)/8,(F(2+4t)-1)/8 are isometries Z2->Z2, thus finite quotient permutations and surjections, implying exactly one odd-index preimage for each even output and four even-index preimages for each target ≡1 mod8. Periodicity follows from 1-Lipschitz. Independently checked all 8184 integer index residues for k=3..12; unrestricted law is from the analytic argument. k=1,2 are explicit boundary cases.
